source_reviews.independent_solution: A dynamometer measures force through spring deformation proportional to elastic force in the same spring's linear working range. Deformation is displacement from the unloaded baseline, not total spring length or successive increments with changing baselines. A calibrated pointer maps deformation to force. It can measure different force types, not just a hanging mass's gravity.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Fix the spring upper end to a paper-covered board; attach the hook/rod and moving pointer to the lower end. Establish unloaded zero, then settled positions under known total forces. At g=9.8 N/kg, mass 1/9.8 kg gives exactly 1 N; 102/204/306 g give approximately 0.9996/1.9992/2.9988 N. Total mass matters: 102 g plus another 204 g is about 3 N, not 2 N. Fixed guides do not replace a moving pointer; arbitrary equal marks do not establish an absolute force calibration.

source_reviews.independent_solution: A grip dynamometer measures hand squeeze through compression of an oval spring and pointer mechanism. A suitable-range traction dynamometer in the pulling load path measures large pulling forces, such as tractor traction. Dial angles and unprovided numeral units are not universal force calibration; co-motion does not change force measurement into speed. The unitless 0..5 traction dial cannot determine a newton value or exact capacity from the class's tens-of-thousands-of-newtons description.
